published: 2021-03-18T08:57:36Z
summary: Here we survey the compactness and geometric stability conjectures formulated by the participants at the 2018 IAS Emerging Topics Workshop on {\em Scalar Curvature and Convergence}. We have tried to survey all the progress towards these conjectures as well as related examples, although it is impossible to cover everything. We focus primarily on sequences of compact Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature and their limit spaces. Christina Sormani is grateful to have had the opportunity to write up our ideas and has done her best to credit everyone involved within the paper even though she is the only author listed above. In truth we are a team of over thirty people working together and apart on these deep questions and we welcome everyone who is interested in these conjectures to join us.

title: Analysis and Control of Autonomous Mobility-on-Demand Systems
id: http://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14827v2
published: 2021-06-28T16:03:37Z
summary: Challenged by urbanization and increasing travel needs, existing transportation systems need new mobility paradigms. In this article, we present the emerging concept of autonomous mobility-on-demand, whereby centrally orchestrated fleets of autonomous vehicles provide mobility service to customers. We provide a comprehensive review of methods and tools to model and solve problems related to autonomous mobility-on-demand systems. Specifically, we first identify problem settings for their analysis and control, from both operational and planning perspectives. We then review modeling aspects, including transportation networks, transportation demand, congestion, operational constraints, and interactions with existing infrastructure. Thereafter, we provide a systematic analysis of existing solution methods and performance metrics, highlighting trends and trade-offs. Finally, we present various directions for further research.

title: Control Strategies for Autonomous Vehicles

================

This module is the mechanical rulebook for WAKE✳︎.

The model is allowed to PROPOSE changes to durable state.
It is never allowed to decide whether those changes are valid.

That distinction is central to the experiment:

    model output = proposal
    governance = authority
    durable state = accepted history

The functions in this file are deliberately deterministic. Given the same
state and the same proposal, governance should reach the same decision
regardless of which model produced the proposal.

A model cannot persuade this module, reinterpret its instructions, waive a
requirement, or edit the rules during an invocation.

A research transition is atomic: an invalid research action rejects that
transition without partial writes. application_policy.py owns the separate
editorial wrapper, which can withhold an invalid final blog while committing
independently valid research. Do not move that exception into the reducer.

This gives WAKE✳︎ an important property:

    failure can become durable information
    without failure becoming durable state.
"""

non-research execution proof, and [installation boundaries](installations.md) for
independent records and runtime lifecycles. These remain inside this repository.

The local [improvement application](improvements.md) uses that same kernel contract
in an explicitly new experiment record. Captured public research informs code
proposals; it does not become writable research authority. Untrusted candidate
code runs only in restricted disposable containers, while the host scores its
outputs. An operator review receipt cannot apply code or grant release authority.

The [autonomous context lane](autonomous-context.md) is a separate WAKE application
policy on the existing per-node native authority. An installed capability permits
one selector-field change, gated by recomputed fixed-task and current-native-state
measurements. Proposal generation, adoption and rollback require no per-change
human review. Metadata events preserve research versions and history; candidate
data cannot replace the evaluator, widen permissions, modify code or create a
competing research store. Native replay owns the policy after restart.

For a first installation, follow [the simple setup guide](setup.md#1-local-docker-installation).

This page explains the operating contracts and retained compatibility launchers.

## Run one installation container

The current local path is one `wake` container, one web server, and twelve internal
worker processes called nodes. Three parents (`100.wake`, `200.wake`, `300.wake`)
each have three children. Nodes do not run their own web servers. The installation
controller starts, stops, and routes them; they cannot continue after it exits.
Each node retains its own governed SQLite record. The controller has no separate
writable group research database.

Prepare topics and provider settings, then build and launch from the repository:

```sh
test -f .env || cp .env.example .env
test -f research-topics.toml || cp example.research-topics.toml research-topics.toml
# Configure GEMINI_API_KEY if you intend to enable Gemini later.
# Edit your local research-topics.toml for this installation.
./scripts/wake_installation build
./scripts/wake_installation start
./scripts/wake_installation shell
wake-research --help
wake-research status
```

**Every container launch starts research stopped.** Inspection does not enable
research or Bob calls. The Console and shell are available first;
use `wake-research start` only after inspecting the installation and configuration.
The launcher neither pulls source nor switches branches. VS Code can attach to the
running `wake` container; `/workspace` is writable and the existing WAKE `.bashrc`
terminal prompt is retained.
